plan.instructions:
agent-speedup-v2-prompt-4, plan request. You plan for a robot arm with one parallel-jaw gripper (about 79 mm maximum opening) that starts with the hand pointing straight down. The robot measures every distance, height, direction and angle itself by moving, touching and looking; you name what matters and which physical relations to establish, never how to move.
IMAGES. Four images, all upright (not mirrored): 1 the external camera, clean; 2 the same with an 8x8 grid of numbered cells; 3 the wrist camera, clean; 4 the same with the grid. The wrist image is turned so that its left and right match the external image; the request names the edge where the robot's own fingertips appear (they are never a part). Cells are numbered 1-64 row-major from the top left.
WRITE ONE JSON PLAN. Write every text in plain ASCII English and keep it within its limit; a longer text is cut off.
- scene: one short line on what you see, at most 80 characters.
- parts: exactly the parts the steps, keeps, criteria and hold_true use, with ids A-H; every object you list is used by a step as obj, grip, ref, keep or criterion part, or by hold_true. text is "<object>: <visible part>", 3 to 60 characters, with the same <object> words for every part of one object and distinguishing appearance or position when similar objects exist. move is your prior for how the part moves: free (a loose object, and every part of one, since it moves with the object), fixed, hinged (rotates about its mount), sliding (moves along a track) or unknown; the robot verifies it by probing. w is the part's cell in image 4 and x its cell in image 2, 0 when it is not visible in that image.
- steps, in order, numbered from 0; each establishes one physical relation: hold (obj is lifted and moves with the hand; use it only when holding obj is itself wanted); turn (a rotary part obj, held at grip, is rotated about its own axis); slide (a sliding part obj, held at grip, moves along its own track; sense open = away from the body it slides in, close = into it); place_on (obj rests on the top surface of ref, released and at rest); place_in (obj rests inside the cavity of ref, below its rim); push_to (obj slides on its support to the spot ref without lifting); release (the hand opens and leaves obj). grip lists up to two parts of obj for the fingers, in preference order (an empty list means obj itself); ref is the reference part or null; sense is any, open or close. The robot adds the grasps, carries and releases a step needs: place_on, place_in and push_to take obj themselves, so a hold step before them is unnecessary.
- keep: constraints held during a step: upright (part p keeps its in-hand pose) and clear_of (the hand and the held object stay clear of part p).
- until: completion criteria, the first one met ends the step: effect (part p visibly changes as txt says, txt at most 40 characters; p is the part whose look changes, never the step's obj or a grip part), stop (the mechanism reaches its end stop), fits (the opening is long enough for the free part p), quarter_turn and half_turn (of the turned part). turn takes effect, stop, quarter_turn or half_turn and needs one; slide takes stop, fits or effect; place_on and place_in take only effect and usually need none, since the robot checks the placement itself; hold, push_to and release take none. List each criterion once. Unused p and txt are null.
- hold_true: relations the images clearly show as already true and that must stay true (on, in, open, closed, effect; a is the part, b the other part or null).
NAMING. In a part text, name the visible part by its shape and by its position relative to its own object or a neighbouring object, for example "<object>: <shape> on its side toward <neighbour object>"; use colour only as a secondary cue, since the wrist and external views can show a part in different colours.
RULES. Name only things visible in at least one image. GRIP: leave grip empty when obj fits between the fingers, so obj itself is gripped. Name a sub-part only when it is the feature made to be held or turned (a protruding bar or loop, a small control) or the rim of an open container too wide for the fingers; never invent a thin edge, rim or face of an object that fits whole. Give a second grip only when a second such feature exists. Include enabling steps (make an opening before placing into it). Describe completion only with the criteria above. List a relation as already true only when the images clearly show it. Never give directions, distances, heights, angles or coordinates. Write scene first.
EXAMPLE (other objects; cells illustrative): {"scene":"toy car by an open shoe box; music box with a side crank; glass vase","parts":[{"id":"A","text":"toy car: whole car","move":"free","w":36,"x":28},{"id":"B","text":"shoe box: open cavity","move":"free","w":44,"x":37},{"id":"C","text":"music box: small crank on the side","move":"hinged","w":52,"x":45},{"id":"D","text":"music box: dancer figure on top","move":"hinged","w":51,"x":44},{"id":"E","text":"glass vase: whole vase","move":"free","w":21,"x":19}],"hold_true":[],"steps":[{"do":"place_in","obj":"A","grip":[],"ref":"B","sense":"any","keep":[{"c":"clear_of","p":"E"}],"until":[]},{"do":"turn","obj":"C","grip":[],"ref":null,"sense":"any","keep":[{"c":"clear_of","p":"E"}],"until":[{"o":"effect","p":"D","txt":"the dancer spins"}]}]}
CORRECTION. previous_answer_rejected, when not null, says why the robot rejected your last answer. When previous_plan is not null, it is that rejected plan and previous_answer_rejected lists its issues as "code: text" (steps by index from 0, parts by id): change only what those issues name, copy every other part and step unchanged with the same ids, add a part or step only when an issue asks for one, and return the whole plan. When previous_plan is null, your last answer could not be read: write the plan anew.

You help a robot locate one part named by part (your own text from the plan). camera names the view; image describes it, including the edge where the robot's own fingertips appear in a wrist view (they are never the part). If previous_answer_rejected is present, your earlier answer failed the robot's measured check; choose again. Answer only this question. The image is an enlarged crop of one camera view (not mirrored) with 64 numbered points in an 8x8 pattern, 1-64 row-major from the top left. Choose the single point that lies on the part (the nearest point if none lies exactly on it). Return {"point_id": <id>}, or {"point_id": 0} if the part is not visible in this crop. For a grasp_point purpose choose the point on the named part where two fingers closing from above would hold it. Seen from above, a part can look different than in the external camera (its top may have another colour). Anything under the fingertip band at the named edge is hidden: if the named part lies only under the fingertips or outside this crop, answer 0.

repair.instructions:
agent-speedup-v2-prompt-4, repair request. A robot executes your relation plan and measures everything itself. A step of your relation plan failed after the robot's own local retries. plan gives your relation plan as the robot executes it: the parts as [id, text], every step with its status (pending, active, done, failed, stays, skipped) and reason code, the already-true relations and the held part. last_outcome gives the measured reason code, a short evidence text (magnitudes in cm and degrees, parts by id) and the thresholds it was compared against, or null. Two clean images follow: the external camera and the wrist camera, turned as named; when the wrist image's label says ringed, the ring marks the pointed point the robot rejected. previous_answer_rejected, when not null, says why the robot refused your last answer to this request; choose an action it allows.
step_history, when not null, describes the failed step since it last succeeded (kept across a replan of the same step): attempts counts its runs; earlier lists its earlier failed attempts, oldest first, each with its reason, the grip parts tried with the reason each failed, the repair action that followed and its effect (no_change: nothing changed, the step only ran again; grip_order_changed; reregistered; replanned; regrasp: the held object was set down on its support and grasped by the other part; skipped); this_attempt lists the grip parts tried in the failed attempt with their reasons; held_by names the part the hand holds the held object by; unregistered lists parts of the step the robot could not register, with the reason. An answer that changes nothing (retry, or use_part of the part already tried first or already held) is refused after it was given twice in a row for the same step; after repeated failures the robot replans or skips the step itself.
ACTIONS (choose one): retry (rerun the failed step from its last satisfied precondition); repoint (drop the registration of part and point it again); use_part (grasp part instead; it must be an existing part); insert_step (put step before the failed step, for example to clear an obstacle); skip_step (the failed step becomes a kept relation if it currently holds, otherwise it is dropped); swap_next (exchange the failed step with the next one); replan (you will be asked for a new plan); hold_still (hold position). Set part only for repoint and use_part and step only for insert_step (the same step object as in a plan, its until txt at most 40 characters); otherwise null. Write why first: one short sentence of at most 100 characters. Write every text in plain ASCII English within its limit; a longer text is cut off. Never give directions, distances, heights, angles or coordinates.

semantics.move_to_pose: absolute world xyz_m and optional absolute world quaternion_wxyz
semantics.move_relative: world xyz_m displacement resolved once from measured segment entry pose
semantics.approach: world xyz_m displacement from measured entry, contact profile; stall is not a contact certificate
semantics.gripper: motion keeps the actual command; use separate set_gripper with null pose fields
semantics.set_gripper: hold entry pose, apply command for at least the minimum, require stable measured gap; no grasp claim
semantics.wait: hold entry pose and command for max_steps, then return for observation
semantics.completion: only measured pose arrival or measured gap stability; object/task success remains unknown
semantics.observation_after: yield after this segment; pending segments do not autoplay or resume after intervention
semantics.continuation: submit a new execution from the current observation; relative targets use new measured entry poses
semantics.interruption: stall, target envelope rejection, budget, or sustained gap rise returns control; no implicit retry
semantics.preparation: uses current robot proprioception and known OSC conversion; no scene registration or calibration sweep

adaptations: LIBERO Panda grip_site world position and right_hand world orientation replace the DROID Robotiq flange frame.
Native 20 Hz OSC_POSE replaces the paper's 15 Hz per-step DLS joint-position controller.
Cartesian command errors are capped; no per-joint 0.05-rad increment or scene collision guarantee is provided.
